newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expects U.N. probe to go ahead in Congo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expects U.N. probe to go ahead in Congo.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it expected the Democratic Republic of the Congo to allow a U.N. probe into alleged massacres to go ahead on July 7, although U.N. officials said this now looked unlikely.

An advance U.N. team in the capital, Kinshasa, said on Sunday the government of President Laurent Kabila had rejected two non-negotiable terms for the investigation, set down in April in a resolution of the U.N. Commission on Human Rights.

The main body of researchers was due to arrive on July 7 to investigate allegations that Kabila's forces or their allies killed Rwandan Hutu refugees before toppling President Mobutu Sese Seko in May. But a U.N. spokesman, John Mills, said on Monday they were unlikely to make it.

"We believe that (U.N.) Secretary-General (Kofi) Annan should explore all options to ensure that an investigative team travels to the Democratic Republic of the Congo by approximately July 7, as agreed," a State Department spokesman said.
"We expect President Kabila to honour his commitment to allow the team to begin its work on time," the spokesman, John Dinger, told reporters.
"So far there is no delay, because their investigation was not scheduled to start for another week or so," he added. "We expect the investigation to go forward as planned."

The United States has repeatedly warned Kabila that he will not get Western aid to rebuild his country, formerly Zaire, unless he makes progress on democracy, free markets and human rights and clears up the massacre allegations.
Kabila has denied that any massacres took place.
